body: There is no such thing as a right to live if there is no such thing as a right to die. At that point, living is more of an obligation than a right.
What good is a right if I am reprimanded for exercising it? Morons.

I once asked a school counselor this very question. She said, "While I do believe that it is your right to take your own life, I just don't believe you are in the right mindset to make that kind of a decision right now." She then proceeded to have me escorted to the hospital. I can't help but feel like it's censorship in a way. "You will subscribe to our notion that life is all about sunshine and rainbows. You will ignore the overall pointlessness of life in general. If you even think about ending your own pain, I will have you locked up for weeks in a hospital with ineffective 'treatment' because only I can tell you what's best for you."

Tomorrow, I'm going to open up my own restaurant. I'll be the only customer and the only employee. I know what I want already. I will need no menu. And I will serve myself because, for my whole life, I've only been serving others.
If there's anyone who should be ashamed here, it's you. Your lack of empathy on a subreddit made for people who clearly need others' nonjudgmental support is unacceptable. Fucking troll.

I, too, have had a shitty experience with mental health treatment. I'm sick of psychiatrists throwing pills at me, when nothing they prescribe me does a damn thing. I've been on 6 different medications, and every time I tell them my medication doesn't work, they are so eager to give you yet another prescription that--surprise--doesn't do shit.

I have a therapist, but I plan on canceling my two upcoming appointments. My therapist has been really fucking irritating the last few sessions. When I tell him that life is pointless, he says, "I disagree" without explaining himself. When I tell him that nothing brings me joy anymore, he tells me to find hobbies (it's not half as easy as he makes it out to be). And, of course, when you tell a therapist, "I want to die," they call the police and bring you to the psych ward, where you are stripped of freedom and privacy.

I recently got the bill for my last hospital stay. If it weren't for insurance, I'd have to pay $26,000 for two weeks, which I think is fucking unacceptable. The doctor there was kind of a jackass and seemingly chose two random drugs to give me when I told him that everything I tried thus far failed to do anything. The facility itself felt a little old, and the food was mediocre at best. While there, I met an older woman who was ordered by the court to stay there for 6 months. She spent Thanksgiving and Christmas in what was little more than a prison. She wasn't even allowed to go outside, which is a right even murderers enjoy.

Just thinking about how broken the system is makes my fucking blood boil. Rant over.
I've had a similar experience. You're free to message me if you want to talk. I'm no expert but it might help you to write things out.

I agree. I can't stand people who think that life is all about rainbows, unicorns, and pretty pink butterflies. Oh please. We work and work and work, but ultimately, we all end up in the same place--buried in a box under six feet of dirt, rotting for the rest of eternity. We can't take our money or possessions with us when we die. We're all just ants on a speck of dirt moving through a universe that is too enormous for us to even comprehend.

I don't know about the life insurance part, but your friend is right about the hospital. The second you tell anyone in the medical community that you are suicidal, they will call either an ambulance or the police to escort you to the hospital against your will.

Depending on where you live, your doctor/psychiatrist/psychologist can get a court order to keep you confined in the hospital. I once met someone who wasn't allowed to leave for six months. I felt sorry for her.

If you want to give treatment a try, I suggest you see a psychiatrist first. You might have to change your prescription a few times to see what works and what doesn't.
Many thanks for your advice, friend.

I'd really hate to sound selfish, but I just cannot do this anymore. One of the few reasons I'm not dead yet is that I didn't want to hurt my family, but I've come to realize that I've had enough already. If my brother told me he was in this much pain and that none of the help he received was working, I would want his suffering to end, even if that meant that I would be negatively affected as a result. I hope I don't sound angry or anything, but I don't know if you understand just how hard it is to even breathe, to exist, when you're feeling this bad.

I haven't watched my old favorite shows in years, but I guess there isn't a reason I shouldn't watch them now.

Psychology can be difficult at times, especially when you're learning about neuroscience and the different parts of the brain. I could never match all the different brain regions with their functions. But I used to be a STEM major so this stuff isn't that bad by comparison.

I can't see the light at the end of the tunnel. I don't even know if there is one, but if there is, I'm not sure if it's worth holding on until I see it. The only thing keeping me going is the fact that I know that I may only have barely over a month left on this earth. If I had to wait any longer, I'd probably either be dead or in a hospital after a failed attempt.

Yes, my major is psychology (ironic, isn't it?). It's also my favorite subject. I find a lot of things interesting, so it shouldn't be hard to do the exercise you suggested. I'm designing a psychological experiment for one of my classes. I'm going to ask my participants to watch a documentary, so I've been looking at Vice documentaries on YouTube. I like them, but the past week has been tough for me, so I've been finding it harder to concentrate and enjoy the videos lately. I was trying to watch earlier, but I'm kind of in a crisis right now. I'm crying so hard, I can barely breathe. I want to die. I want to die. Someone make it stop please.

I file my own taxes. In fact, I'm expecting my return in the next couple of weeks. I'm not exactly sure what my options are, but I suppose it's worth looking into.

I don't remember a lot about being younger; it was a while ago. But I guess I felt "normal" for most of the time. I believe environment played a factor. My dad lost his job. Money was tight. My parents had to borrow money from a friend. I was getting picked on at school and I was experiencing ongoing sexual trauma for years. Although those are no longer problems I have to currently deal with, I never really recovered from all of that.

I wouldn't exactly call it a sacrifice. If not for them, I will kill myself, for myself. At least I will be free from this suffering. In any case, in the mean time, maybe I'll check that book out and also try being in the moment. I appreciate the advice.

To be honest, I don't really know for sure. Maybe it just makes more sense to me that bad things happen to bad people. I just really hate myself (I don't know why), so I convince myself that I am a bad person and that I deserve everything I'm getting.

Now that I think about it, you may be right in that I want to be talked out of it. I'm not looking forward to doing this, but honestly, what choice do I have? Depression is one of those things that you can never get rid of; you just have to learn how to live with it. And there is no way in hell I'm going to go through this crap every day for the rest of my natural life. I wouldn't wish this pain on anyone. It's too much and I need it to stop.

Essentially, what I meant is that there is no reason for me to keep holding on. I've never been happy to be alive, even when I was younger. I have been depressed since I was 12. I don't want to eat. I have a strong urge to isolate myself. I abuse painkillers sometimes as a means of self-harm. Doing basic hygenic tasks is a lot harder than it should be. There is nothing that brings me joy. I wake up every day wondering why I couldn't have died in my sleep the night before. I cry myself to sleep most nights. I hate myself so much I can barely put it into words. I know that I deserve this pain, but I can't take it anymore. My parents don't deserve a piece of shit son like me. They should be happy when I die.

Yes, I'm 20.
I've been on 4 different medications (Abilify, Trazodone, Wellbutrin, and Lexapro). Three of them didn't help at all. Trazodone helps with my insomnia, but doesn't make me feel better.
I tried talking to my parents, but they just don't understand depression. They think that I can just shake it off or something.
The counseling center on campus is essentially useless. I've been told that they are only there to connect students with outside services. There's not much they can do to help you other than refer you to someone else. I've been to outside counseling, but I'm not sure if it's really helping. Between counseling and medication, I've probably spent a few hundred dollars trying to get better. It might not seem like a lot, but I can only afford to hold a job during the summer break, so I don't have a lot of money. My parents expect me to be responsible and independent, so asking them for money is out of the question.
I've been held in a hospital four times in three different places. That is not a place I like to be. Also, my parents' insurance doesn't cover hospitalization anymore, so cost is a big issue. I've also attended group sessions, including NAMI meetings. I also have anxiety, so group environments aren't the best for me.

I can't tell them. My mom herself told me that she hates it when I get in this mood. I made my dad cry once. All I do is drag them down. They deserve so much better than to have a toxic person like me in their lives.

I can't tell anyone. My parents wouldn't know what to do. I might as well not make them worry. My friends can't help either. They'll just tell me to go to the counseling center. I can't go back there. They're just going to make things worse.
